_comment: Maximum finding counts per tool. A ratchet: scripts/lint_ratchet.py fails when a
run finds MORE than max_findings, and fails when a commit RAISES max_findings
(against the merge base with main) without a `Ratchet-Exempt: <why>` trailer.
When a run finds fewer, lower the number in the same change to lock the gain in.
Measured 2026-09-19 at commit abf97db, unchanged at a0e4951 (after the ruff safe autofixes and
the 3aecd16 MCP logging fix, which removed mypy's 20 call-arg errors):
ruff  451 findings over 103 files -- ANN001 110, E501 98, ANN202 89, W293 43,
mypy  46 errors in 18 files, 59 source files checked -- import-untyped 10,
No eslint entry, on purpose. frontend/ has no eslint.config.* and eslint 9
refuses to run without one (exit 2 before inspecting a single file), so the CI
lint step has never inspected anything. .gnomon/ci.sh reports it SKIPPED with
that reason rather than inventing a rule set to measure. Whoever adds the config
adds an `eslint` entry here in the same change (tool = eslint, cwd = frontend,
args = ["src/"]); until then lint_ratchet.py refuses to run an undeclared entry.
The args are the SAME ones the tool runs with here and in .gnomon/ci.sh, so the
number and the command that produced it cannot drift apart.

ruff-scripts._why: The gate scripts themselves. Zero, and it stays zero: a gate whose own code does not lint is not one to trust. Ruff's default rule set (no project config at the repo root).
